newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Senate confirms Raines as budget chief.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Senate confirms Raines as budget chief.

text.p: The U.S. Senate Friday confirmed Franklin Raines to be White House budget director.

Raines, 47, was confirmed on a voice vote. He has been vice chairman and director of Fannie Mae and a spokesman there said he will assume his new post as director of the Office of the Management and Budget next week. Raines succeeds Alice Rivlin, who is now vice chairman of the Federal Reserve.

Testifying in July before the Committee on Governmental Affairs, which approved his nomination, Raines said the job of the budget director was "to actually deliver on the promise the administration and Congress have made to the American people to balance the federal budget by 2002 and reduce the burden of the national debt."
